In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of the processes involved in mitochondrial biogenesis, and in particular with the evolution of mitochondrial protein import.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
protein and tRNA import are highly conserved in eukaryotes.
protein import is a very early invention in the history of mitochondria and that tRNA import evolved later, but that both are present in most extant eukaryotes.
the evolution of mitochondrial protein import pathways is a complex story.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
protein import has evolved from a simple process in hydrogenosomes and mitosome to a complex one in mitochondria, whereas the import of tRNA has remained simple in all eukaryotes.
protein import is the more ancient process, and that tRNA import is the more recent process.
the two import systems are highly conserved in eukaryotes and that the evolution of mitochondrial genomes has little effect on their evolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the evolution of the import machinery is intimately connected to the evolution of the organelle itself.
